text:
tess (support): forwarding a customer report from @acme_csr — they saw duplicate side-effects when the model tried to call our send_email tool. they hit it in prod this morning, billing customer unhappy.
acme_csr: hey, our users got the same email twice after their message triggered a summary+send flow. we only send once server-side. attached logs show two tool invocations.
acme_csr: relevant excerpt:
```
REQUEST: {"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"please email summary","tool_call":{"name":"send_email","arguments":"{\"to\":\"user@acme.com\",\"body\":\"...\"}"}}
RESPONSE 1: 202 Accepted {"operation_id":"op-abc123"}
RETRY triggered by client due to timeout
RESPONSE 2: 200 OK {"result":"ok","sent_id":"msg-789"}
LOG: invocation=send_email request_id=req-42 status=OK sent_id=msg-789
LOG: invocation=send_email request_id=req-43 status=OK sent_id=msg-790
```
maria (support): they claim our system executed the tool twice (different sent_id). looks like the LLM fell back to non-tool (generated a manual email body) and we ended up sending both? unclear.
raj (eng-oncall): can you paste the exact API payload + headers (client side) and any retry-after / timeout behavior? also which model + runtime? (dedicated or hosted)
tess (support): forwarding more from their devs:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"gpt-redwood-1",
    "input":"Summarize and email",
    "tool_call":{
      "name":"send_email",
      "arguments":"{\"to\":\"user@acme.com\",\"body\":\"summary...\"}"
    }
  }'
# client library retried on 504/timeout using exponential backoff (default)
```
satoshi (eng-ml): a few possibilities: 1) client got 202 and retried the full request which re-triggers tool invocation server-side; 2) our fallback policy ran (model generated a direct email) after the tool path timeout; 3) no idempotency key in tool arguments so two successful executions create distinct sends.
maria (support): they said they saw a 202 on first try and then a 200 on retry. also a fallback email body appears in the second response payload (llm-generated) — so both the tool and the non-tool path produced actions.
raj (eng-oncall): immediate ask: can we see the request logs for that customer for window 2023-10-12T08:00:00Z -> 08:05:00Z? correlate request_id -> operation_id -> tool exec. tess can you share customer_id and approximate times privately.
tess (support): done, sent IDs: op-abc123, req-42, req-43. customer uses hosted API in us-west.
raj (eng-oncall): quick hypothesis: our runtime treats 202 from tool runner as "accepted but not completed" and returns to client. client retries the whole generation -> we run the model again, model doesn't call tool or does -> different behavior. the critical bug: missing server-side idempotency enforcement for tool invocations invoked by the same generation request when there's an overlapping retry.
satoshi (eng-ml): agree. also fallback policy currently will synthesize an action if the tool loop times out. if a retry later succeeds we end up with both. fix path: 1) ensure tool invocations are deduped by operation_id or idempotency_key created at request acceptance; 2) change client recommendations: don't retry on 202, instead poll operation_id; 3) add a provenance flag in sent emails: source=tool vs source=llm to detect duplicates.
maria (support): customer is asking for a mitigation now — they want us to stop duplicates immediately if possible.
raj (eng-oncall): short-term mitigation we can do from backend: add a 5-minute dedupe window keyed by (customer_id, recipient, subject, maybe hash of body) for email tool to suppress obvious dups. can we toggle for this customer only?
satoshi (eng-ml): yes we can add a feature-flagged dedupe in the email adapter quickly. will need DB write + quick rollback. not ideal long-term but reduces customer pain.
maria (support): also propose adding idempotency guidance to docs and sample SDK change: include an explicit "idempotency_key" in tool_call.arguments or top-level request.
tess (support): sent a temporary workaround to customer: 1) ask client to stop retrying on 202 and instead poll operation endpoint; 2) add idempotency_key to tool args; 3) we flagged them for the backend toggle. they accepted.
raj (eng-oncall): action items:
- raj: enable customer-scoped dedupe toggle on email adapter (ETA 2h)
- satoshi: design server-side idempotency via operation_id canonicalization (ETA EOD)
- maria/tess: update support reply + docs snippet and escalate billing/comp for duplicate sends (ETA 1d)
- eng-oncall: instrument more logging for tool execution path and fallback decisions (low overhead)
maria (support): logs we need from infra: correlation of generation request_id -> model decision path (tool vs text) -> tool run operation_id -> final status. also timestamps for client retries.
raj (eng-oncall): deploy-bot: rolling deploy flagged patch to email adapter under feature-flag for customer acme_corp.
deploy-bot: queued deploy to us-west pool (canary 1/5).
raj (eng-oncall): I'll watch logs during rollout.
satoshi (eng-ml): long-term design note: tool_call schema should include explicit idempotency_key and an enum for desired semantic (fire-and-forget / await-completion / pollable). that prevents ambiguous 202 semantics.
maria (support): customer follow-up: they want a one-off credit for duplicated sends. cc finance via support ticket.
acme_csr: thanks — appreciate the quick response. will monitor and confirm once dedupe is live.
raj (eng-oncall): thanks everyone. if we get repro steps from their devs that reliably trigger duplication please paste here (short commands appreciated). next update in 2h.
acme_csr: their dev forwarded a minimal repro script (they said it's non-sensitive):
```
# minimal repro loop
for i in 1 2; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"email summary","tool_call":{"name":"send_email","arguments":"{\"to\":\"user@acme.com\",\"body\":\"x\"}"}}' &
done
```
acme_csr: they ran concurrent retries after a 202 and saw two sends.
tess (support): copying in mitigation checklist to the ticket. closing this thread for now but will update when dedupe toggle is live.
maria (support): noted follow-up: file a postmortem if duplicate sends > 3 for any customer in the next week.
raj (eng-oncall): ack. monitoring alerts set for duplicate-send-rate spike for email tool.
